name: POST /api/leadflow/leads/:id/accept - the owner takes the lead, without buying more time
description:
Records that the assigned rep has the lead. THE RESPONSE CLOCK RUNS FROM WHEN THE LEAD ARRIVED, not from when its current owner got it. Every handover moves assigned_at and leaves source_timestamp and sla_due_at exactly where they were. That is enforced in three places on purpose: a BEFORE UPDATE trigger in migration 024 RAISES if source_timestamp changes, so an offending UPDATE fails whoever wrote it and whichever path it came through; no statement in ownershipService writes that column; and every handover records the clock it saw into leadflow_ownership_event, which makes the invariant checkable after the fact rather than only assertable at the time. The natural implementation breaks this by accident - reassign sets assigned_at = now(), somebody later recomputes sla_due_at from assigned_at to keep it consistent, and a rep who takes over a breaching lead inherits a fresh clock while the breach vanishes from the report.

ACCEPTING IS NOT A NEW LEAD. It stamps accepted_at and touches nothing else about the clock - the customer has been waiting exactly as long as they were a second earlier, and an accept that extended the deadline would let a rep reset their own SLA by clicking a button (b736b718-a31c-4ac3-a9ef-1a65613dcff5#AC1).

IDEMPOTENT. accepted_at uses COALESCE, so a double-clicked button or a retry after a timeout keeps the FIRST acceptance instant. The first accept is when the rep actually picked it up, and a second call must not rewrite that.

ONLY THE CURRENT OWNER MAY ACCEPT. The UPDATE is scoped to owner_user_id, so a rep accepting a lead that has since been reassigned away from them matches no row and gets a 404 rather than silently stamping somebody else record.

THE HAPPY PATH IS 404 here: the suite registers a throwaway user who owns no leads, and no environment seeds one assigned to them. The refusal branch is the real one worth holding - it proves acceptance is scoped to ownership rather than open to anybody with the id. QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: Accepting a lead the caller does not own is refused
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: No lead assigned to you with that id
errorCases.when: the lead does not exist, or is not currently owned by the caller. One code for both, deliberately: telling a caller that a lead exists but belongs to somebody else discloses the existence of a record they have no claim on.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
